To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The atmospheric state vectors derived from radiosondes launched 1h and 5 min prior to IASI overpasses are consistent within one IASI instrument noise.

the IASI instrument noise is a significant factor in the interpretation of IASI observations, that the radiative transfer models considered are in good agreement with the IASI observations, and that the radiosonde data used to derive best estimates of the temperature and humidity atmospheric state vectors are of sufficient quality to be used for this purpose.
The atmospheric state vectors derived from RS92 sondes launched 5 min before the IASI overpass and extrapolated to the IASI over pass time are the best estimate of the atmospheric state vector.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: 1) What is the accuracy of the atmospheric state vector obtained from radiosonde measurements?
the validation of IASI radiance observations using radiosondes.
the development of the atmospheric retrieval algorithm, the retrieval of atmospheric profiles and the validation of the retrieved profiles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the IASI measurements and the radiative transfer model calculations match to within the noise level.
the IASI measurements are in agreement with the radiosonde measurements, the radiative transfer models used, and that the radiosonde data are of sufficient quality for the purposes of this study.
the radiative transfer models used in this study are able to simulate IASI radiances to within the noise level of the IASI instrument.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the best agreement is found when using LBLRTM 11.6 with the temperature best estimate profile and the humidity dry bias corrected profile, while the best agreement for the humidity profile is found when using OSS with the temperature best estimates.

the radiative transfer models are in general agreement with IASI measurements, but that the best estimates of the state vectors need further improvements, especially with respect to the humidity profile.

the IASI measurements and the calculated radiances are in good agreement, and that the best estimate atmospheric state vectors are a reasonable representation of the true atmospheric state vector at the time and location of the IASI overpass.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IASI observations are in good agreement with the radiosonde data and the radiative transfer models used.
LBLRTM version 11.3 and OSS are the most accurate radiative transfer models in this spectral region.

, in order to match the IASI observations, the radiative transfer models need to use a temperature profile that is colder by about 0.5 K at the surface and by about 0–1 K at 300 hPa, and a humidity profile that is wetter by up to 10% at the surface and drier by up to 5% at 300 hPa.
